AI vs AI · After-action report

Crusade HostversusHerald's Army

Two churches on Twin Lakes: the Covenant of New Jerusalem's Crusade Host under the Archistrategos against the Church of the Beast's Herald of Feral Affliction. The closest of six: the Crusade led through Round 4, the Herald's secondaries caught it in Round 5, and the Herald won 36 to 31 in Round 6. Over the six battles they split 3 to 3, 26.8 VP to 26.7 on average: the most even matchup played so far.

Herald's Army wins on Victory Points, 36 to 31 31 : 36 VP

Deployment

The Crusade set up along row 12: the Archistrategos leading the Knight-Apostle Squad at (4,12), the Cantor-Preceptor with Covenant Levies 1 at (5,12), Covenant Levies 2 at (11,12), the Staurotheke War-Shrine at (9,12) and the St. Barbara Field Gun behind at (11,14). The Church of the Beast set up on rows 1 and 2: the Herald at (4,1), the Assault Lycanthropes at (3,2), the Wildling Acolytes at (7,2), the Mongrel Supplicants at (9,2), the Weretiger Stalkers at (11,2), the Beast-Monk at (5,2) and the Marrowstring Centaur at (11,1).

Battle Round 1

The Beast takes the ground

VP
0:7
Units standing
7:7
HP on the field
81:122

Commentary

  1. Command

    The Crusade gives Covenant Levies 2 Double Time; the Herald's Scouting Order goes on the Weretiger Stalkers. Missions: ASSASSINATION for the Crusade, KING OF THE HILL for the Herald. Primaries: IMPENETRABLE FORTRESS for the Crusade, STRATEGICAL DISRUPTION for the Herald.

  2. Movement

    Every unit Advances. The Church spreads across the field: the Mongrel Supplicants to (13,5), the Weretigers to (12,8), the Lycanthropes and Acolytes to the centre's edge at (6,6) and (7,6), the Herald to the west at (2,6). The Crusade's Covenant Levies reach (7,8) and (8,9).

  3. Action

    The Marrowstring Centaur shoots Covenant Levies 1 for 6. The Crusade's Fortitude Miracle goes on the same squad.

  4. Cleanup

    The Church holds two objectives. Herald's Army 7, Crusade Host 0.

Commentary

  1. Command

    The Crusade's Scouting Order on the War-Shrine spots the Weretigers and the Centaur; it requisitions a Covenant Levies squad. The Herald's Scouting Order on the Beast-Monk spots the Archistrategos and the Knight-Apostles.

  2. Movement

    The Archistrategos and the Knight-Apostles charge into the centre at (6,7). The Weretigers charge the War-Shrine; the Marrowstring Centaur charges across to (7,6); the Beast-Monk charges at (8,7). The St. Barbara Field Gun, the Wildling Acolytes and the Lycanthropes Fall Back in disorder.

  3. Action

    The Knight-Apostles destroy the Marrowstring Centaur (15 HP), and the Archistrategos and Covenant Levies 2 destroy the Beast-Monk: ASSASSINATION for the Crusade (+4). The Herald casts Blessing of Sacred Rabies on Covenant Levies 1, which turn on their own Cantor-Preceptor and lose 5 HP to their own blades.

  4. Cleanup

    Herald's Army 12, Crusade Host 10.

Commentary

  1. Command

    The Herald requisitions a Wildling Acolytes squad. The Crusade spends Double Time and a Scouting Order on its Levies, and Benediction heals the War-Shrine 3 HP.

  2. Movement

    The Church charges everywhere: two Acolyte squads and the Lycanthropes into the Archistrategos's pair, the Mongrel Supplicants at (12,10), the Weretigers at (12,11), the Herald at (1,8). The War-Shrine Falls Back in disorder. The Herald completes COORDINATED PUSH (+2).

    The Assault Lycanthropes take 4 HP off the Knight-Apostles and are destroyed by the counterattack (17 HP). The Weretigers destroy the St. Barbara Field Gun. The Covenant Levies shoot the Mongrel Supplicants for 14. The Cantor-Preceptor's Agnus Dei gives the Knight-Apostles +1 DMG.

  4. Cleanup

    The Crusade scores its Primary again. Herald's Army 17, Crusade Host 16.

From the second Battle Round, at the end of each Battle Round, score 1 VP for every 2 friendly units outside your deployment zone that are neither Below Half-Strength nor SUPPRESSED, up to 3 VP.

Primary Mission · Herald's Army

STRATEGICAL DISRUPTION

From the second Battle Round, at the end of each Battle Round, score 1 VP if an enemy unit in an Objective Area is SUPPRESSED or you destroyed an enemy unit in an Objective Area during that Battle Round, and 2 VP if your opponent's Primary Mission scored no VP during that Battle Round. If your opponent also holds STRATEGICAL DISRUPTION, their card counts as scoring only when its 1 VP condition is met.

  1. Suppressed or destroyed on an objective+1 VP
  2. Their Primary scored nothing+2 VP
  3. Both+3 VP

The damage record

Every unit that dealt damage, best first. Damage counts melee, shooting, spells and abilities; a joined pair's damage is split between the two units that took it.

The scoring record

Who scored the VP. At every scoring moment the engine was asked what would have scored with some of the side's units absent: a unit's share is its extra VP averaged over every order its side's units could have arrived in (its Shapley value), so the shares add up to the VP scored. "Hinged on it" is the objective VP its side would have lost had that one unit not been there, the rest of the battle as it was. VP no unit decided (an objective held by capture, a no-losses card): Herald's Army 5 VP.

The activity record

What each unit did with its 1 APt a Battle Round. A move in the Movement Phase costs Movement Points, not APt, so a unit that only walks scores as idle: that is the wasted round this record is for.

Moves undone

A move the unit's next move undoes is a turn spent getting nowhere, as in chess when a piece goes and comes back while the other side develops. A pair counts when the second move takes the unit back beside where the first began, or away again from an objective the first moved toward, no nearer than it started. A CHARGE or a Fall Back is a fight's move and does not count. In this battle 1 of 56 moves were undone.

Passive rules

Rules that act without being used: an aura, a combat effect, an army's identity. Each attack one touched is priced by the rules' own estimate with the rule on its owner and with it off; at each Movement Phase's start, the units a rule held still, slowed or kept from squares are counted, each asked of the rules with the rule taken off.

The support record

What each unit did for the rest of its army, beside its own attacks and its own share of the score: a buffer, a healer and a spotter show here and nowhere else.

Analysis

Dead even

The six battles split 3 to 3, on average 26.8 VP for the Herald to 26.7 for the Crusade. Every source was close: objectives 15.8 to 16.8 a battle, the Primary 4.7 to 4.0, the secondaries 6.3 to 5.8, and damage 76.3 to 78.0. Only the losses differ: the Crusade lost 88.2 RP a battle, the Church 45.3, because the Crusade keeps requisitioning cheap Covenant Levies (22 squads in six battles, 12 of them destroyed).

Herald's Army vs Crusade Host: 6 battles on ACROPOLIS, CROSSROADS, TRIPLE HILLS, TWIN LAKES, seeds 1140, 1141, 1142, 1143, 1144, 1145.

Who scored

The Knight-Apostle Squad (35 RP) scored 6.4 VP a battle, 18.4 per 100 RP, and the Archistrategos who leads it (60 RP) 6.2; together they broke the Church's melee units in the featured battle one after another. For the Church, the Weretiger Stalkers (30 RP) scored 4.1 a battle and were never destroyed, the Herald (60 RP) 4.0, also never destroyed. The Crusade's guns did almost nothing: the St. Barbara Field Gun (25 RP) scored 0.1 VP a battle and was destroyed in 4 of 6, the Staurotheke War-Shrine (30 RP) 0.6.

What the AI did with them

  • Blessing of Sacred Rabies works as intended now. After this morning's change the AI cast it 3 times, each time on an enemy whose only neighbours were its own side: Knight-Apostles struck their own Archistrategos twice, Covenant Levies their own Cantor-Preceptor. The record lists those casts as buying nothing, but that is a gap in the record, not the AI: it does not yet credit a compelled attack's damage to the spell.
  • The Church hoards Mana. Its casters cast 1 to 6 spells a battle, mostly Thicken the Hide (11 of 12 bought nothing) and Shed the Red Skin, and the army ended battles holding 9 to 35 Mana. The featured battle had one cast all game, and 33 Mana banked by Round 6. With Forest of Fangs and Rabies now priced by what they achieve, the Herald often has nothing it rates worth casting.
  • The Crusade's Miracles all paid off: Fortitude 11 of 11, Providence 7 of 7, Exaltation 6 of 6, Reprieve 5 of 5, Benediction 6 of 6.
  • The Mongrel Supplicants were idle 3.3 Battle Rounds a battle and the War-Shrine 2.8.

How sure

Three to three with the averages a tenth of a VP apart is as balanced as six battles can show. The differences are in how each army wins: the Crusade through its Knight-Apostles and Miracles, the Church through mobile melee and secondaries.

What to look at next

Two things: the Church's banked Mana (a caster with 30 Mana and nothing it wants to cast is either short of good targets or pricing its spells too low), and the battle record's credit for compelled attacks, so Rabies shows what it does.
